comments.content: The refactored `processStream` no longer handles the `assistant.enableWebSearch` link conversion logic that existed before (convertLinks/convertLinksToOpenRouter/convertLinksToZhipu/convertLinksToHunyuan). The new `convertLinksMiddleware` only calls `convertLinks(chunk.textDelta)` unconditionally, dropping the provider-specific converters (OpenRouter, Zhipu, Hunyuan) and the `isFirstChunk` argument. This is a functional regression for web-search-enabled models from those providers. Please restore the provider-specific conversion logic (or extend the middleware to accept a converter function).

`getAppropriateTag` always returns `reasoningTags[0]` (i.e. `think`) regardless of the model — the `claude` branch is dead code. If the intent was to use `reasoning` for some models, this is a bug; otherwise remove the misleading branch.

`THINKING_COMPLETE` is only emitted inside the `text-delta` case when `time_thinking_start > 0 && time_first_content_millsec === 0`. If the model produces reasoning but no subsequent text (e.g. stream ends after reasoning, or only tool calls follow), `THINKING_COMPLETE` is never emitted. The previous implementation emitted it via `isReasoningJustDone`. Consider emitting `THINKING_COMPLETE` on `finish` if reasoning was produced but no content followed.

`processToolUses(content, idx)` and `BLOCK_COMPLETE` are now invoked inside the `finish` case of the switch. If the upstream stream ends without ever yielding a `finish` chunk (e.g. paused via `CHAT_COMPLETION_PAUSED`, or a provider that omits `finish_reason`), `processToolUses` and `BLOCK_COMPLETE` will never fire. The previous code called them after the for-await loop unconditionally. Move these calls outside the loop (after the for-await) to preserve behavior.

The stream transform never flushes the remaining `buffer` on stream close. If the stream ends while `buffer` still contains text (e.g. partial tag or trailing content), that text is silently dropped. Add a `flush` handler to the TransformStream that publishes any remaining buffer.

`readableStreamAsyncIterable` does not release the reader lock or cancel the stream when iteration is aborted early (e.g. `break` in the for-await). Consider implementing `return()` on the iterator to call `reader.cancel()` / `reader.releaseLock()` to avoid leaking the underlying stream.
